text:
maya_support: URGENT - ACME prod seeing repeated 504/5xx from hosted inference since 09:02 UTC. P95 latency spiked, multiple customer requests timed out. Sample error: `req_id=acme-9f3a 504 gateway_timeout downstream=kvcache_queue_full`

maya_support: Dashboard snapshot: https://dash.redwood.internal/tenant/ACME/queue?range=15m -> queue_depth peaked at ~980 (limit 800), continuous-batcher backlog growing, many longseq requests (3k-8k tokens) in flight. Customer is blocked. Please triage and propose immediate mitigations. @liam_oncall @arjun_sre

deploy-bot: deploy status: No recent deploys to hosted-ingress in last 2 hours.

liam_oncall: On it. Can you paste tenant id + a repro curl? Also any signs of auth/billing errors earlier?

maya_support: Tenant: ACME-prod (tenant_id: t-acme-0042). Repro curl (from customer):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" 
 -d '{"model":"rwd-8k","input":"<long_input>","max_tokens":1500}'
```
They also noted a burst of retries starting ~09:01 where their client rotated keys and got some 401s before switching keys. Could be contributing to retry storm.

arjun_sre: I see the same in infra metrics: continuous-batcher queue_time and backlog_count jump at 09:01 coincident with a tenant spike. KV cache miss rate climbed (suggests cold KV cache for many longseqs). Root contributors: (1) tenant traffic spike w/ large seqs, (2) retry amplification from auth failures, (3) queue depth cap hit causing early dequeue slowdowns -> cascading tail timeouts.

arjun_sre: Immediate mitigations I recommend (safe, low-risk):
- apply per-tenant ingress throttle: `rate_limit_rps=20` for t-acme-0042
- reduce continuous-batcher `batch_window_ms` for model `rwd-8k` to 5ms in hosted routing for this tenant to favor latency over packing
- enable fallback routing to `rwd-3b-fast` for requests with seq > 2k tokens
- temporarily bump queue depth soft limit to 1100 if capacity available (monitor)

nina_platform: I can push the routing changes and fallback via the control plane. Increasing soft queue depth requires manual capacity check (we have spare pods in gpux-pool-3). Any objection?

liam_oncall: No objections. I'll apply throttle + batch window patch now and watch. Also will contact infra to spin one additional gpux instance if tail persists. Executing admin call:
```
POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/admin/tenants/t-acme-0042/throttle 
{ "rps": 20 }
```

maya_support: Customer-side note: they confirmed their SDK retried ~5x on 401s before switching keys; they've fixed key rotation and will avoid immediate retries. Marking that as contributing factor. :+1:

deploy-bot: config-change: `batch_window_ms` for rwd-8k updated to 5ms for tenant t-acme-0042 by nina_platform at 09:06 UTC.

arjun_sre: After throttle + batch_window change: p99 tail reduced from ~4.2s to ~820ms within 3 minutes. 504s stopped. KV miss rate still slightly elevated but decaying.

nina_platform: I pushed fallback route to rwd-3b-fast for longseqs. Also filed infra request to add 1 gpux to gpux-pool-3 (ticket INFRA-8431).

liam_oncall: Confirming no new 504s in last 12m for ACME. Rolling back temporary bump to queue depth once warmup finishes. I'll keep the per-tenant throttle for 30m then re-evaluate.

maya_support: Customer update: ACME confirmed service restored and thanked support. Raised follow-up request about cost impact (routing to smaller model) and asked for root cause summary. Support ticket: SUP-2026.

arjun_sre: Action items:
- write short postmortem (owner: arjun_sre) covering auth-retry amplification + batching interaction
- add a runbook entry: auto-apply tenant backpressure if queue_depth > 750 for > 30s (owner: nina_platform)
- consider making `batch_window_ms` tenant-configurable in Console (owner: nina_platform)

nina_platform: I'll schedule a follow-up with the ACME CSM and file a PR for console change.

liam_oncall: Closing ops loop for now. Monitoring dashboards for 1h and will update SUP-2026 and incident notes. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
